text: 🇲🇽✊ 26,000 homes delivered. Housing is a right, not merchandise. "We're going to hold a 'Housing Wednesday.'" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, launching a weekly housing link Over 26,000 homes have been delivered across 98 developments under the Housing for Wellbeing program. The first weekly link went to Ahome, Sinaloa, where 96 families received keys. One beneficiary: a two-bedroom apartment, and no more rent.

🇲🇽🌎 The treaty doesn't die today. No panic. "If the US doesn't decide to extend for 16 years today, the treaty stays in force for the next 10 years — its full term, until 2036. It's not that the treaty ends; the 10 years continue, with reviews." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the USMCA (T-MEC) review June 30 was the deadline for a joint 16-year extension. Mexico and Canada signed; the US didn't. Under Article 34.7, the deal runs to 2036 regardless, with annual reviews. Mexico is also opening other trade agreements.

🇲🇽🌎 "An embassy is like a small piece of your territory." "An embassy is like a small piece of [our] territory." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on relations with Ecuador In April 2024 Ecuadorian police stormed Mexico's embassy in Quito to seize a former vice president who had been granted asylum — a breach of the Vienna Convention. Mexico cut ties. Asked about restoring them, Sheinbaum was open to dialogue but firm on the principle Ecuador broke.

🚨🇲🇽 "What proof do they have?" "The people this statement names were already under investigation by our Financial Intelligence Unit. They rushed ahead with their announcement — they didn't wait for joint coordination. What proof do they have?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on new US Treasury sanctions Washington sanctioned Mexican individuals and companies unilaterally, without informing Mexico. Cooperation, yes — subordination, no.

🇲🇽🎨 A free public university for history, feminism, and popular resistance. "[A model] to form students with solid academic preparation, critical thinking and social conscience — through public, free, quality education." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the new INEHRM The new institute opens degrees in History and Public Administration, and master's programs in Mexican Humanism, Gender Studies and Feminisms, and Social Movements. Free diploma courses cover migration, popular resistance, human rights, and AI & the humanities.

🇲🇽🎨 "History is part of the living memory of a people." "History is not a catalogue of dates nor a succession of illustrious names. History is part of the living memory of a people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, signing the INEHRM decree The decree turns the Institute of Historical Studies of Mexico's Revolutions into a research and teaching body under the Science and Humanities Secretariat. History as a living tool of the people — not a shelf of bronze statues.

🇲🇽✊ Eight years ago today, the people won. "Eight years ago was the triumph of the Fourth Transformation of Mexico's public life — July 1st. And the way to honor it, the triumph of the people, is this Institute dedicated to history." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the 8th anniversary of the 4T On July 1, 2018, Mexico elected AMLO and began the Fourth Transformation. Eight years on, Sheinbaum marked the date by signing a decree that turns the national historical-research institute into a public university.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICAN EXPORTS JUMP 25.4% — HIGHEST MAY ON RECORD, FIVE STRAIGHT MONTHS OF GROWTH

INEGI reports exports hit 69.5 billion dollars in May, up 25.4% year-on-year — the strongest May since records began — with non-oil, non-auto manufacturing up 38%. The trade balance stayed in surplus at 2.26 billion dollars, and the first five months of 2026 close at a 5.77 billion dollar surplus, against just 918 million in the same period last year. The "tariffs will crush Mexico" narrative keeps running into the data and losing.
